why: Large clinical ECG study showing intersectional performance disparities and limits of representation balancing.

authors: Maria Galanty; Bjorn van der Ster; Alexander P. Vlaar; Clara I. Sanchez
why: Closest verified ECG sex-bias classification paper; demonstrates persistent MI disparities even with balanced training.

title: Understanding the Effect of Model Compression on Social Bias in Large Language Models
why: Controlled evidence that quantization and distillation change BERT/RoBERTa social-bias measurements and utility trade-offs.
evidence: Evaluates DistilBERT/DistilRoBERTa and quantized BERT/RoBERTa/Pythia with CrowS-Pairs, StereoSet, and SEAT. Distillation lowers measured social bias but can substantially reduce language-model score; results are representational-bias evidence, not clinical EO.

title: Improving Group Fairness in Knowledge Distillation via Laplace Approximation of Early Exits
why: Recent BERT-to-DistilBERT group-fairness KD method based on uncertainty-weighted difficult examples.
evidence: Uses bert-base-uncased, distilbert-base-uncased, and MultiNLI. The preliminary study reports modest potential and explicitly calls for more datasets, group definitions, and hyperparameter testing.
